draft.title: Other traditions before 1945
card: Christianity was not the only religion in Australia before 1945. Other traditions came with groups of people who settled or worked here.
Jewish communities
Jewish people arrived from the early years of British settlement, including some on the First Fleet. They practised Judaism and built community life in colonial towns and cities.
Muslim cameleers
From the 1860s, cameleers from Afghanistan and British India worked in inland Australia with camel teams. They were Muslims, and they brought Islam to the outback.
Chinese miners
Many Chinese miners came to the goldfields in the 1850s. They brought beliefs and practices from China, and some built temples.
draft.remember: Jewish settlers, Muslim cameleers and Chinese miners each brought their own religious traditions to Australia before 1945.

a.q: Which group brought Islam to inland Australia in the 1800s?
opts: Cameleers from Afghanistan and British India
Miners who came to the goldfields from China
Jewish people who arrived on the First Fleet
Church of England chaplains sent from Britain
a.why: Cameleers from Afghanistan and British India were Muslims who worked with camel teams in the outback. The Chinese miners also came for work, but they brought beliefs and practices from China, not Islam.
a.clue: Think about who worked with camels in the outback.

b.q: In 1858, Wei travels from southern China to work a claim on the Victorian goldfields. What is he most likely to bring with him?
opts: Religious beliefs and practices from China
The Muslim faith of the Afghan cameleers
The Church of England practices of colonial officials
Jewish customs from the First Fleet settlers
b.why: Chinese miners on the goldfields brought beliefs and practices from China, and some built temples. The Muslim faith is linked to the cameleers, who worked in a different part of Australia and came from different places.
b.clue: Which tradition is linked to people from Wei's homeland?

a.best: Cameleers from Afghanistan and British India

b.best: Religious beliefs and practices from China

problems.detail: 'They were Muslims' overgeneralises. Most cameleers were Muslim, but some from British India were Sikhs or Hindus. Better: 'Most were Muslims'.

The question is too easy for Year 11. The distractors make no sense for a man arriving from China: he cannot 'bring' the cameleers' faith, First Fleet customs or colonial officials' practices. The question also says Wei comes 'from southern China' and only the right option says 'from China', so students can match the words without knowing the idea.
The why says the cameleers 'worked in a different part of Australia'. The card does not teach this, and cameleers did later serve goldfields, for example in Western Australia in the 1890s.

check.summary: The facts are mostly sound, but the card overstates that all cameleers were Muslims. Question b is too easy because the wording and the implausible distractors give the answer away, and its why adds an unsupported claim about where cameleers worked.

proposal.title: Other traditions before 1945
card: Christianity was not the only religion in Australia before 1945. Other traditions came with groups of people who settled or worked here.
Jewish communities
Jewish people arrived from the early years of British settlement, including some on the First Fleet. They practised Judaism and built community life in colonial towns and cities.
Muslim cameleers

From the 1860s, cameleers from Afghanistan and British India worked in inland Australia with camel teams. Most were Muslims and brought Islam to the outback, but some from British India were Sikhs or Hindus.
Chinese miners
Many Chinese miners came to the goldfields in the 1850s. They brought Chinese religious practices, which mixed Buddhist, Taoist and Confucian ideas, and some built temples.
proposal.remember: Before 1945, Jewish settlers, cameleers and Chinese miners brought religious traditions other than Christianity to Australia.

a.q: Which group brought Islam to inland Australia in the 1800s?
opts: Cameleers from Afghanistan and British India
Miners who came to the goldfields from China
Jewish people who arrived on the First Fleet
Church of England chaplains sent from Britain
a.why: Most cameleers from Afghanistan and British India were Muslims, and they worked with camel teams in the outback. The Chinese miners also came for work, but they brought Chinese religious practices, not Islam.
a.clue: Think about who worked with camel teams in the outback.

b.q: Which statement about other traditions in Australia before 1945 is accurate?
opts: Some cameleers from British India were Sikhs or Hindus
Every cameleer who came to Australia was a Muslim
Judaism first reached Australia after Federation
Chinese miners built no temples on the goldfields
b.why: Most cameleers were Muslims, but some from British India were Sikhs or Hindus. The claim that every cameleer was a Muslim is tempting because they are often called Muslim cameleers, but it overgeneralises. Jewish people came from the First Fleet on, and some Chinese miners built temples.
b.clue: Be wary of statements that say every or no.
